title: Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps

epigraph.quote: “Price is what you pay; value is what you get.”
epigraph.author: Warren Buffett

book_paragraphs: As of the 12 November 2026 close, TD Power Systems traded at ₹625.90, with the TradingView snapshot showing a market capitalization of roughly ₹19,597 crore and trailing P/E of 71.1x; Screener’s same-session card showed 62.0x. The vendors are not perfectly aligned on the earnings denominator or capture time, so the report treats the range as a warning about valuation sensitivity rather than selecting the lower multiple. The company is valued as a high-growth industrial compounder even though its ten-year record includes losses, cyclicality and uneven free cash flow [1][2][3].

The latest audited year is FY2026: consolidated revenue was ₹1,856 crore, operating profit ₹335 crore and net profit ₹239 crore. The current TTM snapshot advances sales to ₹2,513 crore, operating profit to ₹474 crore and net profit to ₹339 crore, with TTM EPS ₹10.81. At the current close that is roughly 58 times snapshot TTM EPS, while TradingView reports 71 times. Both readings imply that current shareholders are paying many years in advance for a small industrial supplier whose cash conversion is weaker than its income statement [1][3].

The cash-flow cross-check is harsher than the earnings multiple. FY2026 CFO was approximately ₹129 crore and capital expenditure roughly ₹111 crore, leaving about ₹19 crore of free cash flow in the snapshot. That is not a normalized owner-earnings figure: Tumkur expansion and tooling can depress current cash generation, while growth working capital may later release. Yet a market value near ₹19,600 crore against one year of ₹19 crore FCF is not supported by current cash yield. Buyers must underwrite sustained high growth, maintained margins and better collections; otherwise reported earnings and order momentum will not become distributable cash [1][9].

A simple reverse-DCF lens uses the market capitalization as a conservative enterprise-value proxy because the business is nearly debt-free, while acknowledging that a full lease and cash reconciliation is not available in the public snapshot. At a normalized 40x earnings multiple, the market value requires roughly ₹490 crore of annual earnings; at 50x, about ₹392 crore; and at 60x, about ₹327 crore. The last is close to the current TTM ₹339 crore, but it assumes investors will continue to accept a premium multiple after exceptional growth. At 40x, earnings would need to rise roughly 44% from the current TTM level to reach ₹490 crore. A more conventional 30x valuation would require about ₹653 crore, nearly double current TTM profit [2][3].

Those are not price targets. They expose what has to go right. To justify the present value at 40–50x earnings, TDPS needs the export-led order book to convert to revenue without sacrificing its 17–18% operating margin, the new facility to absorb more volume, and new capital not to cause material dilution without a corresponding increase in profit per share. The September 2026 order book of ₹2,318.7 crore and H1 revenue of ₹1,482 crore support near-term visibility, but backlog is not revenue, revenue is not cash, and orders can be delayed or rescheduled [3][4][9].

Peer comparison is difficult because no listed Indian company is a pure-play supplier of customized AC generators across the same OEM mix. Cummins India sells engines and generator sets at a larger scale; Bharat Heavy Electricals is a project-heavy power-equipment integrator; Bharat Bijlee overlaps in electric machines; ABB India and Siemens are diversified electrical and automation platforms. They are reference points for valuation and capital intensity, not interchangeable business models. The snapshot table therefore puts profitability, growth, size, valuation and technical stage in one place rather than presenting a single peer multiple as a fair value [10].

The base valuation framework assumes EPS grows from the snapshot’s ₹10.81 TTM to about ₹16.40 over the next two years, then applies 50x earnings to produce ₹820 per share. This requires roughly 23% annual EPS growth and a premium industrial multiple; it is an optimistic base, not a conservative liquidation value. A bull case of ₹1,100 requires EPS near ₹20 at 55x as orders, new customer programs and margins compound. A bear value of ₹400 assumes earnings around ₹10 and a 40x multiple, reflecting a growth pause and multiple compression. The wide range is more decision-useful than a single-point DCF because cash flows are currently distorted by growth capex and working capital [1][3][4].

The forecast should be judged against three observable gates. First, quarterly order inflow must remain broad enough that one OEM or one data-centre cycle does not dominate. Second, operating margin must hold near the recent high teens even as export mix and larger generators rise. Third, cash conversion must improve: receivable days should stop rising, inventory should not outgrow production, and CFO should converge toward PAT over a rolling multi-year period. A missed revenue guide is less damaging than a pattern of revenue beating estimates while cash conversion deteriorates [1][2][9].

The practical conclusion is that the market already discounts meaningful future execution. The company may deserve a premium to capital-goods peers because it has engineering qualifications, global reach and a strong backlog. It does not yet deserve a blank cheque: its visible aftermarket stream is small, top-ten customer concentration is high, and the current cash yield is negligible. We use ₹820 as an illustrative two-year base value and insist on a pullback toward the ₹590–₹600 structural shelf before considering new capital. That entry would reduce the price risk and leave a base-case reward greater than the defined stop distance; it would not remove the business risks [1][3][9].

When you and I compare TDPS with peers, the first adjustment is for scale and mix. Cummins India manufactures engines and generator sets with a much broader service base; BHEL bids large, long-duration power projects where contract execution and receivables dominate; Bharat Bijlee sells motors and engineered electrical products; ABB and Siemens combine equipment, software and automation. Their multiples are not a clean answer to what TDPS is worth. They are useful bounds: the market should reward specialized engineering and exports, but it should also discount a small supplier whose order flow is concentrated in a few global platforms. The peer table is a compass, not a valuation model.

A second valuation trap is to extrapolate the most recent quarterly growth rate. H1 FY2027 revenue was ₹1,482 crore and the September quarter was strong, but one quarter can reflect customer delivery timing, order mix or milestone recognition. To earn a 50x multiple, TDPS must deliver growth across multiple years, not merely pull sales forward. We would want to see the next two reported quarters maintain order inflow while preserving margin and customer terms. If backlog falls because shipments are catching up, that is healthy only when collections follow. You should read the income statement and cash-flow statement together, not let a large sales print close the question.

The valuation is also sensitive to dilution. The company raised capital through a QIP and promoter preferential allotment during its expansion phase. Equity issuance can be sensible when a company is funding a capacity bottleneck with attractive returns; it can also reduce each existing share’s claim if capacity is slow to ramp. The useful measure is not simply total profit growth, but EPS and cash flow per share after new shares and capex. A future report should calculate that bridge from the audited share count, capital employed and realized utilization. Until then, the ₹820 base value carries execution risk that a low-debt balance sheet alone cannot remove.

A fair-value range should be updated when the capital structure changes. TDPS is nearly debt-free in the latest snapshot, which limits interest-rate risk, but it does not eliminate equity risk. New shares, leases on facilities, export receivables and customer advances all alter the claim on future cash. The next analyst should reconcile cash and lease liabilities from the audited filing, use diluted shares after the QIP, and calculate enterprise value consistently before refreshing the reverse DCF. The present analysis avoids false precision where the same-session data vendors show different trailing P/E readings and does not treat the quoted price as the exact value of the operating assets.

Valuation sensitivity is the main weakness in the entry case. The ₹820 base value uses analyst EPS of ₹16.40 and 50x earnings. Holding EPS constant and reducing the multiple to 40x gives ₹656 (₹16.40 × 40). At a ₹600 entry and ₹520 invalidation, that is ₹56 upside against ₹80 downside, or 0.70:1; at ₹585, it is ₹71 against ₹65, or 1.09:1. Both fail the 1.5:1 hurdle. Therefore the ₹585–₹600 zone is not independently attractive on the 40x stress: a fresh EPS bridge, lower entry, or evidence supporting a premium multiple is required before an order. The present verdict remains WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT and assigns no capital [1][9].

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: A 70-times earnings multiple can be rational only if earnings grow, cash follows earnings and investors keep paying a premium. Ask which of those three assumptions has the strongest evidence today. The answer is order momentum; the weakest link is cash conversion.

web_blocks.the_number: ₹490–₹653 Cr of annual net profit would be required to support the current ~₹19,597 Cr equity value at 40x–30x earnings.
web_blocks.how_calculated: Divide the same-session market capitalization by the chosen steady-state P/E multiple. This is an earnings hurdle, not a discounted cash-flow target.
web_blocks.the_inputs: Current snapshot net profit: ₹339 Cr TTM; market capitalization: ₹19,597 Cr; selected reference multiples: 30x, 40x and 50x.
web_blocks.the_range: At 50x, the hurdle is ~₹392 Cr; at 40x, ~₹490 Cr; at 30x, ~₹653 Cr.
web_blocks.if_off: If growth slows or the market rerates the company below 30x, the equity value can fall even if the business remains profitable.

web_blocks.takeaway: These are imperfect peers. The table is a size and multiple cross-check, not a pure generator-comp valuation; company scale, revenue mix and project risk differ materially.
